text:
simon: quick brain-dump — thinking about a 'soft-probe' admission layer to catch sudden tenant spikes without global eviction. idea: when a tenant's token rate jumps > X within T, we mark the next N requests as probes and score them for abuse signals. keep probes cheap and bounded. any obvious pitfalls?
priya: curious — how do probes differ from existing probation? feels similar but sounds less punitive. what signals does probe collect?
jamal: probes should be readonly and non-blocking for normal traffic. collect latency, error-rate, model score distributions (if available). we need a sampling budget per-tenant so this doesn't become a vector for extra load.
megan: tradeoffs: extra metric collection could add tail latency if routed through inference path. maybe offload sampling to a mirror path (async). also need to ensure probes don't change KV cache warmness.
simon: good point. current thought: mark probe requests with a header `X-Probe: id` and route copies to an async sidecar that does deeper checks (content hashing, n-gram rates, unusual embedding patterns). main path only records lightweight counters.
laura: product note — we must surface probe outcomes in Console as 'soft-safety flags' and tie to tenant alerts. ops wants a rate-limited page so SRE can triage.
jamal: interface question: should the admission service own probe lifecycle (start/stop, budget tracking) or should the ingress edge manage it?
megan: lean toward admission-service owning lifecycle. ingress should just forward probe hints and apply immediate short-term accept/reject. central owner makes consistent probability decisions across regions.
priya: concern: central owner means more RPCs at admission time — could increase P50. Can we make decisions locally using leased budgets synced periodically?
simon: proposal: hybrid — local fast-path consults a cached lease for a tenant. if cache misses or score crosses threshold, fallback to central admission. we can express lease as `probe_budget: { tokens: 5, expires_at: 1670000000 }`.
jamal: sounds reasonable. also add telemetry events: `probe_start`, `probe_result:{pass|flagged}`, `probe_budget_exhausted`. those should be tagged with `probe_id` for traceability.
megan: can we see a compact config example?
simon: sure — quick sketch:
```
admission:
  probes:
    enabled: true
    spike_threshold_pct: 300
    window_ms: 60000
    probe_budget_per_min: 3
    async_sidecar: true
```
priya: nit: `spike_threshold_pct` needs to be tenant-profile aware. an enterprise tenant with steady 10qps vs a free user with 0.1qps behave differently. we should compute relative thresholds (percentile baselines) not absolute values.
laura: also need a human override / whitelist for partners.
infra-bot: synthetic-load test run complete: probe-mode adds ~0.8ms median on ingress when local caches hit, 12ms p99 on cache-miss fallback. results: https://ci.internal/runs/9931
simon: thanks infra-bot — that p99 on fallback is acceptable if we keep fallback rare. next steps: I'll draft an RFC covering lifecycle, telemetry names, and console hooks. volunteers to review?
jamal: happy to take a pass on the lifecycle/consistency section.
megan: I'll review performance impacts and async sidecar sketch.
priya: I'll do thresholding and tenant-profile section.
simon: great — assigning draft to eng-infra RFC board. tagging @channel for visibility. :thumbsup:
laura: thanks — will add console mocks after RFC lands.
megan: tiny follow-up: consider black/whitelist for model-level probes (some models produce noisy evasion signals).
jamal: noted. we'll include model exemptions table in RFC.
simon: cool — closing thread for now, will post RFC link when available. :white_check_mark:
